title: Release Briefing Capsule: Traffic Swarm Editor and Rollback Rehearsal Flow
creator: Maya Alvarez
description: Design a compact, low-friction UI component (the 'Release Briefing Capsule') that surfaces an editable traffic-splitting editor, a micro-simulation preview called the 'Traffic Swarm', and an inline rollback rehearsal experience. The capsule should be embeddable on model release pages and support quick canary setups, A/B variants, and a guided rollback path without leaving the release context.
goals: Provide a single-surface experience to set up canaries or A/B splits in under 60s for power users
Surface likely impact via a fast statistical micro-simulation (Traffic Swarm) that uses recent request distributions and key metrics
Give operators a safe, rehearsable rollback flow with clearly surfaced assumptions and one-click revert rules
Keep the interaction compact so it can slot into release overviews, PRDs, and runbooks
decisions: Embed capsule as a collapsed card by default; expand to a 3-column editor on click
Traffic Swarm simulates at a per-10k request granularity using sampled recent telemetry rather than full-history replay to keep latency low
Rollback actions will create a reversible 'revert transaction' with a human confirmation and optional automated guard (cooldown + conditions)
We will synthesize mock KPI trajectories (latency, error-rate, cost delta) using the runtime's exposure model for preview graphs rather than querying live aggregates during prototype testing
tradeoffs: Micro-simulations prioritize speed over exact fidelity; can produce false negatives for rare-edge regressions
Embedding the editor reduces context switching but adds complexity to release page layout—requires responsive collapse rules
Automating rollback rules reduces operator effort but increases surface for accidental rollbacks; we bias toward human-in-the-loop confirmations for v1
acceptance_criteria: Prototype (Figma + clickable) demonstrates: collapsed capsule, expanded editor, Traffic Swarm panel, and rollback rehearsal modal
PM / Eng signoff that the simulated KPI visualizations map to runtime outputs and that assumptions are documented
Usability test with 5 platform engineers shows median time < 75s to define a 10% canary and run a simulation
Design tokens and responsive rules included so the capsule can be embedded in release overview and incident runbook views
